narrative:
The model estimates an 86% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile that closely match employees who ultimately chose to move on.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook were your total years of experience across all jobs, the length of time you have spent in your current role, and whether you received other job offers while working here. 

Your 11 or more years of overall experience was the single biggest influence pushing the prediction toward leaving. Among people the model expected to stay, only 15% had this much experience, so the system sees long-tenured professionals as more likely to seek new horizons. Your relatively short time in this specific organization (1–5 years) added further weight in the same direction; most employees the model predicted would stay had either spent longer in their current place or were much earlier in their careers. Finally, the fact that you have received other job opportunities also pulled the prediction toward departure, as this is a common early signal that someone is already exploring alternatives.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture of someone who has built substantial expertise but may now be ready for the next step. The organization should discuss your long-term goals with you openly. You, in turn, may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with where you see your career heading.
